name: gb200_multibox
_comment: NVIDIA GB200 multi-rack deployment template. Each rack is one NVL72 island (72-port NVSwitch5, NVLS-capable, 0.5 us SW alpha / 0.2 us INC alpha) stitched by Quantum-2 InfiniBand (SHARP-capable, 2.5 us SW alpha / 0.4 us INC alpha; each compute tray carries four single-port ConnectX-7 400G NICs for its four GPUs, so one NDR 400 Gb/s = 50 GB/s port per GPU). num_devices and ib.ports are auto-overridden by `system_with_eta(num_devices=N)`: ib.ports = ceil(N / 72). Default N=576 (8 racks). Rack chip is Blackwell B200 (192 GB HBM3E @ 8 TB/s, 2250 TF FP16 dense, hbm_eta_beta=0.7). Fabric INC capability is disclosed at the hardware level; whether the runtime engages NVLS / SHARP is a framework decision (`FrameworkSpec.inc_enabled`). For the no-INC counterpart (production stacks that opt out of SHARP) keep this spec and set `inc_enabled=False` on the framework. For an idealized single-tier 576-port crossbar (hypothetical perfect NVL576 fabric), use `gb200.nvl576.ideal.json`; for a rail-optimized 2-tier topology variant (alpha=2.0 us instead of 2.5 us, ib_rail fabric name) use `gb200.nvl576.rail.inc.json`. Checked against the vendor's product page in November 2026: the GB200 NVL72 table lists 720 PFLOPS dense at 4-bit for 72 GPUs (10 PFLOPS per GPU, so 2500 TFLOPs at 16-bit under the byte-ratio rule) and 13.4 TB of HBM3E per rack (186 GB per GPU; 192 GB is the nominal per-GPU figure).
